title: Pivot tables in one sitting
goal: You will turn a sales sheet into a refreshable PivotTable with rows, summed values, a report filter, and a PivotChart.
prerequisites: An Excel sales sheet with column headers in the first row
At least one category column, one numeric sales column, and one column suitable for filtering
No completely blank rows or columns inside the sales data

steps.action: Click any populated cell inside the sales data.
steps.where: Sales worksheet grid in the Microsoft Excel workbook window.
steps.why: Excel uses the surrounding data region as the PivotTable source.
steps.checkpoint: One cell inside the sales data has a green selection border.
hint_levels: Start anywhere within the block of sales records.
Choose a cell below a column header, not an empty cell outside the data.
Click one populated cell in the sales data, such as a cell under Product, Region, or Sales.

steps.where: Insert tab on the ribbon, PivotTable button in the Tables group.
steps.why: This dialog lets you confirm the source data and choose where the PivotTable will go.
steps.checkpoint: The Create PivotTable dialog is visible and the Table/Range box contains a cell range.
hint_levels: Look on the ribbon for the tab used to add new objects.
The PivotTable command is in the Tables group on the Insert tab.
Click Insert > PivotTable > From Table/Range.

steps.action: Create the PivotTable on a new worksheet.
steps.where: Create PivotTable dialog, New Worksheet option and OK button.
steps.why: A separate sheet gives the summary room without changing the source data.
steps.checkpoint: A new worksheet opens with an empty PivotTable placeholder and a PivotTable Fields pane on the right.
hint_levels: Choose the placement option that keeps the summary separate.
Select New Worksheet near the bottom of the dialog.
Click New Worksheet, then click OK.

steps.action: Add a category field to the PivotTable's Rows area.
steps.where: PivotTable Fields pane on the right, field list and Rows box at the bottom.
steps.why: The PivotTable needs categories such as Product, Region, or Salesperson to group its results.
steps.checkpoint: The selected categories appear as row labels in the PivotTable.
hint_levels: Choose the field whose items should run down the left side.
Drag a category field from the field list into the box labeled Rows.
In PivotTable Fields, drag Product, Region, or Salesperson into Rows.

steps.action: Add the numeric sales field to the Values area.
steps.where: PivotTable Fields pane on the right, field list and Values box at the bottom.
steps.why: The Values area calculates a total for every row category.
steps.checkpoint: A numeric column labeled Sum of Sales or a similar field name appears in the PivotTable.
hint_levels: Find the field containing the amounts you want to total.
Drag the numeric Sales or Amount field into the Values box.
In PivotTable Fields, drag Sales, Revenue, or Amount into Values.

steps.action: Change the value calculation to Sum if Excel chose another calculation.
steps.where: PivotTable Fields pane, dropdown beside the field in Values, then Value Field Settings dialog.
steps.why: Summing produces sales totals instead of counting the number of records.
steps.checkpoint: The PivotTable value heading begins with Sum of and the cells show total amounts.
hint_levels: Check the heading above the PivotTable numbers.
Use the value field's menu to choose how Excel summarizes it.
In Values, click the field dropdown > Value Field Settings > Sum > OK.

steps.action: Add a field such as Region or Year to the Filters area.
steps.where: PivotTable Fields pane on the right, field list and Filters box at the bottom.
steps.why: A report filter lets you show one subset of sales without rebuilding the PivotTable.
steps.checkpoint: A filter name and dropdown appear above the PivotTable.
hint_levels: Choose a field that would be useful for narrowing the report.
Drag a field from the list into the box labeled Filters.
In PivotTable Fields, drag Region, Year, or Salesperson into Filters.

steps.action: Select one item from the report filter.
steps.where: Filter dropdown above the PivotTable, beside the filter field name.
steps.why: This confirms that the PivotTable can display a chosen subset of the sales data.
steps.checkpoint: The filter cell shows the selected item and the PivotTable totals update.
hint_levels: Look directly above the row labels for a dropdown arrow.
Open the report filter and choose one listed item.
Click the filter dropdown above the PivotTable, click an item, then click OK.

steps.action: Refresh the PivotTable after returning the report filter to All.
steps.where: PivotTable Analyze tab on the ribbon, Refresh button in the Data group.
steps.why: Refreshing pulls current values and new records from the source data into the summary.
steps.checkpoint: The filter displays (All), the PivotTable remains visible, and Excel finishes refreshing without an error.
hint_levels: Select the PivotTable to reveal its special ribbon tabs.
Reset the filter to (All), then find Refresh on the PivotTable Analyze tab.
Choose (All) from the filter dropdown, click inside the PivotTable, then click PivotTable Analyze > Refresh.

steps.action: Insert a PivotChart for the PivotTable.
steps.where: PivotTable Analyze tab on the ribbon, PivotChart button in the Tools group, then Insert Chart dialog.
steps.why: A PivotChart turns the summarized sales totals into a visual that stays linked to the PivotTable.
steps.checkpoint: A chart appears on the worksheet with category labels and plotted sales values.
hint_levels: Use the chart command on the PivotTable-specific ribbon tab.
With the PivotTable selected, open PivotChart and choose a common chart type such as Clustered Column.
Click inside the PivotTable > PivotTable Analyze > PivotChart > Column > Clustered Column > OK.
